secrets.name: github_focx_write_token
secrets.usedFor: GH_TOKEN on every agent with git: write

gitWrite.GIT_CONFIG_VALUE_0: !f() { [ "$1" = get ] || exit 0; host=; while IFS='=' read -r k v; do [ "$k" = host ] && host="$v"; done; [ "$host" = github.com ] || exit 0; echo username=x-access-token; echo "password=$GH_TOKEN"; }; f

repo-worktree.comment: A git worktree per issue, cut from the Connect project's checkout. baseRef MUST be remote-tracking: Paperclip only fetches when the ref parses as <remote>/<branch>, so a bare 'develop' silently branches from whatever the local checkout happens to be. cwd is deliberately absent — the claude ACP lane ignores it, and the worktree is the workspace.

none.comment: No repository on the filesystem. That, not prose, is what stops a non-technical agent editing application code.

confinement.comment: filesystemScope and networkScope are spawn-level confinement and BOTH require Bubblewrap, which is Linux only (adapter docs: 'filesystemSandboxCommand ... Linux only'). This host is macOS, so they are omitted: setting them makes every run fail with "bwrap was not found in PATH". Without them there is no OS-level sandbox, and the controls that remain are the git tier (who holds GH_TOKEN), each agent's cwd, the CLI's own permission system, and CODEOWNERS plus branch protection.

independence.comment: QA Engineer's independence used to be a separate clone at focx-qa, visible as a distinct cwd. Worktrees replace that with something git enforces: QA works its own child issue, so it gets a different branch AND a different directory from the build it verifies, per issue rather than per agent. The marker moved; the guarantee got stronger.
